questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a university where I could study in French while still doing my exams in English. ULB offered this opportunity.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Brussels is the center of the European Union which was very interesting for me. I have been particularly interested in European Affairs while Brussels seemed the right choice. At the same time it offered a perfect mean to learn French. Both because my subjects were in French and ULB offers many different language courses and offers which helped me a lot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine to find all the information I needed. My host university held some introduction events in the beginning that guided us well through the first days.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Welcoming events and very detailed information from my host university that explained very well what to do and what was expected from me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Was okay avaliable - There are some quite strong student networks that can help finding accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Not really sure what is good to know. Other than it is possible to find good places to live together with other students as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to go there first and get our documents signed. The university had some well functioning systems with different forms which worked fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always text the international office at ULB that almost replied vey quickly and was very good at giving advice needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Worked perfectly. The first two weeks were try out weeks which was a very nice experience because you could try out a lot of different subjects and verify whether it fitted your level. That was a very nice way of organizing the first weeks!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much. I tried to always be ahead on the applications. Most things gets much easier when you arrive to uni. So only do what's asked in the beginning and then deal with the rest at uni. Everything is much clearer once you arrived.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very engaged and talented teachers largely speaking. I learned a lot. However 5 ECTS is very little for a subject which also meant I had to take 6 different subjects to reach 30 ECTS points. This meant that sometimes the subjects didn't have the time or curriculum to go totally in depth. On the other hand I got a good introduction to a very large scale of subjects which was also nice!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching style is quite similar in the teaching room. My classes was mostly structured around a teacher or guest lecturer presenting a subjects and with good oppurtunities for students to ask questions. The difference is tho the level of reading. In Copenhagen there's much more to read and the exam are mostly based on the readings. At ULB the word of the teacher carries as much weight as the very few readings at the uni.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON-S-467 Law and Economics of the Environment
POLI-D-403 L'Europe et la nation (Europe and the nation)
POLI-D-436 Identités, communautés et espaces publics en Europe
(Identities, communities and public spaces in Europe)
POLI-D-538 Armement et désarmement en politique internationale
(Armament and Disarmament in International Politics)
POLI-D-547 Le Brésil : puissance émergente (Brazil: emerging
power)
POLI-D-556 Régimes politiques d’Europe centrale et orientale

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
POLI-D-436 Identités, communautés et espaces publics en Europe
Wonderful course with very interesting guests. A course that really benefits and uses the fact that ULB is in Brussels by inviting very interesting people from the policy world into ULB.

ECON-S-467 Law and Economics of the Environment
A course by two very talented and gifted lecturers that manages to merge to complicated areas into one course that is accessible also for political science students. It is a subject with quite a lot of hands on experience in the fact that the exam takes form in a report and presentation in front of the class. This allowed to apply the theory learned and to get deep into the subject.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Quite a lot of student groups that organized super nice and relevant events.
A bit hard to join them and to find info as an Erasmus student but very easy to join and participate in the planned events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Come to events and really prioritize to participate in the Erasmus events in the beginning. Those are super cool and you get to meet a lot of friends that stays around for the rest of the stay.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the fact that Brussels is so much in the middle of Western Europe. You got trains to Amsterdam, Paris, Cologne, Frankfurt, London, Marseille etc. directly from the train stations in Brussels. That is a very cool add on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Easy for a dane I would say! A beerdrinking warm people that is chill and welcoming.
But definitely (!!) a plus to know the basics in French. Easiest way into the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Hmmm. Try in your classes to talk with co-students - cause that's the place with the most local students to talk to.

I went to Badminton through ULB sports every Tuesday night - That was were I met the most locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Language for sure!
I spoke some french when I started and that helped me a lot. However to really engage it was first towards the end that I got a level high enough to really participate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmth and the excitement of Erasmus students was super nice. Everyone was there to explore and have fun - that creates a super great mood!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Get a very basic French (definitely possible without but huge plus to have)
- Participate in the first Erasmus events
- Don't be shy and reach out to people you've only met once (they usually really want to meet up)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not other than the ones mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: - Meeting other Europeans - was so much fun to share traditions, language and cultures with each other

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The IMMENSE amount of small talk haha!
But was also very given but sometimes you craved a deeper talk with some people that you didn't just meet one month before.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
